record.context_brief: Limits of rewriting for word problems
record.original_question: Is there a decidable uniform word problem for which no variant of rewriting, such as rewriting modulo a congruence with decidable matching or ordered rewriting, can decide the problem without adding new symbols to the vocabulary?

evidence.quote: Is there a decidable uniform word problem for which there is no variant on the rewriting theme that can decide it—without adding new symbols?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and let $\Sigma^*$ denote the free monoid of finite words over $\Sigma$. A finite string rewriting system (Thue system) on $\Sigma$ is a finite set $R \subseteq \Sigma^* \times \Sigma^*$ of rewrite rules $\ell \to r$. The single-step relation $\to_R$ is defined by $u\ell v \to_R urv$ for $(\ell,r)\in R$ and $u,v\in\Sigma^*$; let $\leftrightarrow_R^*$ denote its reflexive, symmetric, transitive closure. The uniform word problem for a class $\mathcal{C}$ of finite rewriting systems asks, given as input a finite system $R\in\mathcal{C}$ over some alphabet $\Sigma$ together with two words $u,v\in\Sigma^*$, whether $u\leftrightarrow_R^* v$.

By a "variant of rewriting" we mean any decision procedure based on rewriting in a generalized sense, including but not limited to:
(i) standard rewriting with a finite confluent and terminating (canonical) system,
(ii) rewriting modulo a finitely-generated congruence with a decidable matching problem,
(iii) ordered (or recursive-path-ordering–based) rewriting using a reduction order,
(iv) any combination of the above using only the original alphabet $\Sigma$ (no auxiliary symbols are introduced into the signature).

Question. Does there exist a finitely presented equational/rewriting theory $(\Sigma, E)$ whose uniform word problem is decidable, but for which no variant of rewriting in the above sense, restricted to the alphabet $\Sigma$ (i.e., without enlarging the vocabulary by introducing new auxiliary symbols), yields a decision procedure for the word problem of $(\Sigma, E)$?
artifact.status_search_result: A classical result of Kapur and Narendran exhibits a finite Thue system with decidable word problem that admits no equivalent finite canonical rewriting system over the same alphabet, while an equivalent finite canonical system does exist if new symbols are allowed. This addresses the case of standard finite canonical rewriting, but the broader question—whether any variant of rewriting (rewriting modulo congruences with decidable matching, ordered rewriting, etc.) can decide every decidable uniform word problem without adding new symbols—does not appear to have been settled in the literature, and is listed among open problems in rewriting.

status_evidence.title: A finite Thue system with decidable word problem and without equivalent finite canonical system
status_evidence.snippet: A single-axiom Thue system is presented with a decidable word problem for which there does not exist any finite equivalent canonical system; an equivalent finite canonical system can be obtained if new symbols are introduced.
status_evidence.claim: Without auxiliary symbols, finite canonical rewriting cannot always decide a decidable word problem; with new symbols it sometimes can.

status_evidence.title: A decidable word problem without equivalent canonical term rewriting system
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of a decidable word problem that has no equivalent canonical term rewriting system.
status_evidence.claim: There exist decidable word problems with no equivalent canonical rewriting system in the same signature.

status_evidence.title: Levels of Undecidability in Rewriting
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of undecidability phenomena and open questions in rewriting.
status_evidence.claim: General questions about the power of rewriting variants for deciding word problems remain open.
